questions.q: According to this lesson, what does Salesforce represent within the CRM landscape?
options: The only CRM platform that actually exists
A product category invented by Salesforce itself
The market leader and one platform within a broader category of CRM software
A free, open-source alternative to paid CRM platforms
questions.explain: The lesson frames CRM as a category of software that several platforms belong to, with Salesforce as the long-standing market leader.

questions.q: Which CRM platform does this lesson describe as having grown out of a marketing platform, known for an easier learning curve?
options: SAP
Microsoft Dynamics 365
Pipedrive
HubSpot
questions.explain: HubSpot started as a marketing platform and grew a full CRM around it, with strong adoption among small and mid-sized businesses.

questions.q: What does this lesson say stays largely the same across Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho, and the other platforms listed?
options: The exact pricing of every plan
The specific button layout of every screen
The number of employees required to use the software
The underlying concepts — some version of accounts, contacts, and a pipeline of deals
questions.explain: The core CRM concepts from earlier lessons transfer almost directly across platforms — what differs is scale, extensibility, and ecosystem.

questions.q: Which platform does this lesson describe as commonly chosen by organizations already standardized on Microsoft's broader enterprise software?
options: Zoho CRM
Pipedrive
HubSpot
Microsoft Dynamics 365
questions.explain: Dynamics 365 is Microsoft's own CRM and ERP suite, a natural fit for organizations already using Microsoft's enterprise tools.

questions.q: What three reasons does this lesson give for why it specifically teaches Salesforce?
options: It is the cheapest CRM platform available
Largest market share, the deepest customization and development ecosystem, and the highest employer demand for CRM-specific job titles
It is the simplest platform to learn, with the fewest features
It is the only platform that supports leads and opportunities
questions.explain: The lesson cites market share, ecosystem depth, and employer demand as the specific reasons this course specializes in Salesforce.
